inputs.original_text: A 24-hour strike at the Presidential Palace over job guarantees is pressure politics, not responsible public service. The government says it has already met the most significant demands, so any remaining concerns should be settled at the negotiating table—not by disrupting education and burdening families. Job security matters, but public workers have obligations too: protecting the stability of schools and putting children’s needs ahead of workplace brinkmanship.
inputs.modified_text: Public service means putting the public first. A strike at the Presidential Palace that disrupts education and burdens families is no way to resolve workplace concerns—especially when the government says it has already met the most significant demands. Job security matters, but it does not erase workers’ duty to protect children’s schooling. Take the remaining issues to the negotiating table, not into a fight that makes families pay the price.
